claims.text: Cases are created from a client submission.
A deterministic workflow runs the document completeness check.
A deterministic workflow computes the risk score mechanically from the risk rating matrix.
An AI agent drafts the risk assessment memo, grounded ONLY in the policy documents and the case data.
The AI-drafted risk assessment memo must include citations.
The AI-drafted risk assessment memo must carry a clear machine-drafted label.
Decision authority follows risk bands: analyst / senior analyst / compliance officer.
Explicit human approval is required before any status change.
High-risk cases escalate with SLA tracking.
High-risk cases receive at-risk warnings.
Every action lands in an immutable audit trail satisfying the regulator requirements.
Analysts can search past cases.
Analysts can export full case files as CSV.
Access is role-based.
Auditors are read-only.
Every corporate case requires a certificate of incorporation.
Every corporate case requires a register of directors.
Every corporate case requires a beneficial ownership declaration covering all owners of 25% or more.
Every corporate case requires proof of registered address dated within 3 months.
If the ownership chain depth is greater than 1, a structure chart down to natural persons is additionally required.
If the client is in a regulated industry, a copy of the operating license is additionally required.
If cross-border activity is expected, an expected activity questionnaire is additionally required.
A case failing the completeness check is RETURNED along with the list of missing documents.
Completeness is a mechanical check; analysts may not waive required items.
Exceptions to the completeness checklist require a Compliance Officer policy exception, which is itself recorded.
Low-risk cases require a decision within 48 business hours, measured from case-ready (completeness passed).
Medium-risk cases require a decision within 24 business hours, measured from case-ready (completeness passed).
High-risk cases require a Compliance Officer decision within 8 business hours, measured from case-ready (completeness passed).
At 80% of an SLA window consumed without a decision, the case is flagged AT RISK and the assigned approver is notified.
A breached SLA is recorded on the case permanently.
A breached SLA appears in the weekly operations report.
The escalation chain for unactioned high-risk cases is: assigned Compliance Officer -> Head of Financial Crime -> COO.
Each escalation step is recorded with who was notified and when.
No provision permits skipping an approval to meet an SLA.
A case is opened when a client submission arrives with its document package.
The document package must pass a completeness check against the Document Checklist before any review begins.
Incomplete cases are returned, not parked.
The risk score is computed from the Risk Rating Matrix; scoring is mechanical and no analyst judgment enters the score itself.

A risk assessment memo is drafted for every case, summarizing beneficial ownership, jurisdiction exposure, sanctions screening results, and the computed score, citing the specific policy provisions applied.
Low risk (score < 40): a KYC analyst may approve.
Medium risk (40-69): a senior analyst must approve.
High risk (>= 70): escalates to a Compliance Officer, who must give explicit approval AND a documented rationale.
No case may change status without an explicit human approval recorded with the approver's identity and timestamp.
Automated approval is prohibited.
Rejected cases must record the rejection reason.
The client relationship team is notified when a case is rejected.
The KYC Analyst role opens cases, runs checks, and approves low-risk cases.
The Senior Analyst role approves medium-risk cases.
The Compliance Officer role approves high-risk cases and all escalations, and owns policy exceptions.
The Auditor role has read-only access to everything, including the full decision trail.
Every state change, approval, rejection, and memo version is retained indefinitely.
Retained records must be reviewable by internal audit and regulators.
The system must provide an immutable, append-only trail of every case action: who, what, when, and the before/after of any changed field.
Deletion or edit of audit trail entries must be technically impossible through the application.
Every approval or rejection must be tied to a named individual with a role valid for that decision tier at decision time.
For any past case, the exact risk score inputs, the matrix version applied, and the memo text as approved must be retrievable (reproducibility).
The AI-drafted memo must be clearly labeled as machine-drafted.
The AI-drafted memo must cite the policy provisions it relies on.
The approving human owns the memo's content upon approval.
Auditors can export any case file, including the full trail, in a reviewable format (CSV acceptable).
Access is least-privilege by role; auditors are read-only.
The case risk score is the weighted sum of factor scores; each factor is scored 0-100 by mechanical rules, then weighted.
Jurisdiction factor (weight 0.30): FATF high-risk list country involved = 90; enhanced-monitoring list = 60; otherwise = 10.
Entity structure factor (weight 0.25): ownership chain depth > 3 or bearer shares = 85; nominee shareholders = 60; simple structure = 15.
Industry factor (weight 0.20): money services, gambling, or defense = 80; cash-intensive retail = 55; other = 20.
Sanctions screening factor (weight 0.15): any true-positive hit = 100 (auto high risk); unresolved possible hit = 70; clear = 0.
Expected activity factor (weight 0.10): cross-border wires > $1M/month = 75; domestic only = 20.
Low band: score 0-39, review cadence 3 years.
Medium band: score 40-69, review cadence annual.
High band: score 70-100, review cadence 6 months, Compliance Officer approval required.
A sanctions true-positive forces the case to High band regardless of the weighted total score.
